prompt: Line up quietly, and I (to give) you five extra minutes outside.
explanation_ru: Повелительное наклонение + «and» заменяет реальное условие в будущем, поэтому во второй части используется «will» + глагол.

prompt: Stop running after the sheep, ___ you will not get a long walk.
explanation_ru: После повелительного наклонения «or» вводит нежелательный результат (если не остановишься). «Without» и «but for» требуют существительного, а не целого предложения.

prompt: You are at Noam's restaurant. The waiter says your main meal is late.
options: Without it is late, the chef will give you a free dessert.
Otherwise, the chef will give you a free dessert.
In that case, the chef will give you a free dessert.
In that case, the chef would have given you a free dessert.
explanation_ru: «In that case» («в таком случае») подходит для реального следствия текущей ситуации; «otherwise» даёт противоположный смысл, а «without» не ставится перед придаточным.

prompt: If my friends do not come on stage, I will not sing. → Without my friends on stage, …
answer: Without my friends on stage, I will not sing.
accepted_answers: Without my friends on stage, I will not sing.
Without my friends on stage, I won't sing.
explanation_ru: Предлог «without» с существительным заменяет отрицательное условие «if ... not», а будущее время результата «will not / won't sing» сохраняется.

prompt: "Are the evening calls finished?" "___, we can go home early."
explanation_ru: «If so» означает «если да» (если звонки действительно закончены). «If not» и «or else» меняют смысл на противоположный.

prompt: Halina gave me her secret dumpling recipe because I helped her cook; without my help, she (to keep) it secret.
explanation_ru: Скрытое условие «without my help» относится к прошлому (она уже дала рецепт), поэтому для нереального результата в прошлом нужна форма «would have + V3».

prompt: Alba finished the front page early, so but for the jammed printer, we (to send) the newspaper on time.
explanation_ru: «But for» («если бы не») в контексте прошлого события требует в главной части «would have + V3».

prompt: Ondřej is panicking in his Prague room; with an earlier start to his revision, he (to feel) much calmer.
explanation_ru: Фраза «with an earlier start» задаёт нереальное условие, а «is panicking» показывает результат в настоящем, поэтому выбираем «would + инфинитив».

prompt: The night bus from Bangkok was freezing, and if it (not / to be) for the thick coat in Jo's backpack, she would have shivered all the way.
explanation_ru: Конструкция «if it hadn't been for» («если бы не») описывает нереальное условие в прошлом и согласуется с «would have shivered».

prompt: Freya closed the coastal road before the tide rose; otherwise tourists (to drive) straight into deep water, and how (we / to reach) them in the dark?
explanation_ru: «Otherwise» здесь вводит нереальные последствия в прошлом («closed», «rose»), поэтому в обоих пропусках нужны перфектные формы с «have + V3», а во втором — вопросительный порядок слов.

prompt: If you do not stay away from the wet river bank, Klara will close the path. → Stay away from the wet river bank; otherwise …
answer: Stay away from the wet river bank; otherwise Klara will close the path.
accepted_answers: Stay away from the wet river bank; otherwise Klara will close the path.
Stay away from the wet river bank; otherwise, Klara will close the path.
explanation_ru: Повелительное наклонение + «otherwise» («иначе») заменяет отрицательное условие «if you do not», сохраняя реальное будущее время «will close».

prompt: Unless you keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, you will pay a fine. → Keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, or …
answer: Keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, or you will pay a fine.
accepted_answers: Keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, or you will pay a fine.
Keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, or you'll pay a fine.
Keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, or else you will pay a fine.
Keep your dog on a lead near the duck pond, or else you'll pay a fine.
explanation_ru: Повелительное наклонение с союзом «or (else)» передаёт предупреждение вместо «unless» и сохраняет «will pay» в части результата.

prompt: If the weak university Wi-Fi did not drop so often, I would finish my online tests calmly. → If it weren't for the weak university Wi-Fi, …
answer: If it weren't for the weak university Wi-Fi, I would finish my online tests calmly.
accepted_answers: If it weren't for the weak university Wi-Fi, I would finish my online tests calmly.
If it weren't for the weak university Wi-Fi, I'd finish my online tests calmly.
If it were not for the weak university Wi-Fi, I would finish my online tests calmly.
If it were not for the weak university Wi-Fi, I'd finish my online tests calmly.
explanation_ru: «If it weren't for» + существительное заменяет нереальное настоящее условие, а главная часть остаётся с «would finish».

prompt: If there were no long delays at the Istanbul departure gate, Selin would enjoy a calm flight and reach home before midnight. → Without any long delays …
answer: Without any long delays at the Istanbul departure gate, Selin would enjoy a calm flight and reach home before midnight.
accepted_answers: Without any long delays at the Istanbul departure gate, Selin would enjoy a calm flight and reach home before midnight.
explanation_ru: Предлог «without» с группой существительного заменяет придаточное «if there were no», а воображаемый результат сохраняет «would enjoy ... and reach».

prompt: If it had not been for Emery's bright torch and calm advice, our camping group would have lost the mountain trail in the dark. → But for Emery's bright torch …
answer: But for Emery's bright torch and calm advice, our camping group would have lost the mountain trail in the dark.
accepted_answers: But for Emery's bright torch and calm advice, our camping group would have lost the mountain trail in the dark.
explanation_ru: «But for» («если бы не») — более лаконичный синоним «if it had not been for» перед существительным; главная часть с «would have lost» не меняется.

prompt: All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon; if they do not, Ms Fraser will not review them. → All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon; if not, …
answer: All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon; if not, Ms Fraser will not review them.
accepted_answers: All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon; if not, Ms Fraser will not review them.
All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon; if not, Ms Fraser won't review them.
All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon. If not, Ms Fraser will not review them.
All candidates must send their job forms to the Glasgow council office by Friday noon. If not, Ms Fraser won't review them.
explanation_ru: Оборот «if not» заменяет целое отрицательное условие «if they do not», избегая повтора глагола.

prompt: Because Ms Aydin organised the roof repairs so quickly, our Ankara school did not have to cancel the indoor sports lessons. → If it hadn't been for Ms Aydin's quick roof repairs, …
answer: If it hadn't been for Ms Aydin's quick roof repairs, our Ankara school would have had to cancel the indoor sports lessons.
accepted_answers: If it hadn't been for Ms Aydin's quick roof repairs, our Ankara school would have had to cancel the indoor sports lessons.
If it had not been for Ms Aydin's quick roof repairs, our Ankara school would have had to cancel the indoor sports lessons.
explanation_ru: Реальный факт в прошлом («did not have to cancel») переворачивается в нереальное прошлое условие с «if it hadn't been for» и «would have had to cancel».

prompt: Check the lorry's fuel level before leaving Rotterdam; ___, you could break down on the motorway.
explanation_ru: «Otherwise» («иначе») связывает инструкцию с нежелательным последствием. «But for» и «without» требуют существительного, а «if so» имеет противоположный смысл.

prompt: "Mr Dimitriou's notice says the terrace is closed for painting next week." "___, let's book a table inside."
explanation_ru: «In that case» («в таком случае») логично реагирует на новость о закрытой террасе. Типичная ошибка — путать его с «otherwise» или «or else», которые означают «иначе».

prompt: The Lisbon coffee shop manager finally gave Beatriz the morning shifts she asked for; otherwise, she ___ her job before summer began.
explanation_ru: Событие уже в прошлом («gave», «before summer began»), поэтому после «otherwise» требуется «would have + V3». Частые ошибки — ставить «will» или забывать «have».

prompt: Without Professor Hamish's help with my draft, I would fail the essay yesterday.
answer: Without Professor Hamish's help with my draft, I would have failed the essay yesterday.
accepted_answers: Without Professor Hamish's help with my draft, I would have failed the essay yesterday.
Without Professor Hamish's help with my draft, I'd have failed the essay yesterday.
explanation_ru: Ситуация относится к прошлому («yesterday»), поэтому вместо «would fail» нужна форма «would have failed» (частая ошибка — опускать «have»).

prompt: Ask your dad to pay for the last toy train before closing time, or else another family will buy it.
answer: Ask your dad to pay for the last toy train before closing time, or else another family will buy it.
accepted_answers: Ask your dad to pay for the last toy train before closing time, or else another family will buy it.
explanation_ru: В предложении нет ошибки: повелительное наклонение + «or else» с «will» правильно передаёт реальное предупреждение о будущем.

prompt: Lucas works at the Lyon town hall; otherwise, he will not know why the central square is closed for the winter market.
answer: Lucas works at the Lyon town hall; otherwise, he would not know why the central square is closed for the winter market.
accepted_answers: Lucas works at the Lyon town hall; otherwise, he would not know why the central square is closed for the winter market.
Lucas works at the Lyon town hall; otherwise, he wouldn't know why the central square is closed for the winter market.
explanation_ru: После «otherwise» описывается нереальная ситуация в настоящем (Лукас на самом деле работает там), поэтому «will not» нужно заменить на «would not / wouldn't».

prompt: Yusra sees a traveller with a very heavy suitcase heading towards a long check-in queue in Doha.
options: Weigh your suitcase at the spare desk first, and you will waste twenty minutes in the queue.
Without you weigh your suitcase first, you will waste twenty minutes in the queue.
Weigh your suitcase at the spare desk first; otherwise, you would have wasted twenty minutes in the queue.
Weigh your suitcase at the spare desk first, or you will waste twenty minutes in the queue.
explanation_ru: Повелительное наклонение + «or» + «will» верно передаёт реальное предупреждение. «And» даёт неверную логику, «without» не сочетается с глаголом, а «would have wasted» относится к прошлому.

prompt: Ingrid's notice at the Oslo community centre says the midsummer fire has moved to the east field, and drivers need a parking pass there.
options: Are you driving to the east field for Ingrid's midsummer fire? If so, please collect a free parking pass at the office.
Are you driving to the east field for Ingrid's midsummer fire? If not, please collect a free parking pass at the office.
Are you driving to the east field for Ingrid's midsummer fire? Otherwise, please collect a free parking pass at the office.
Are you driving to the east field for Ingrid's midsummer fire? But for that, please collect a free parking pass at the office.
explanation_ru: «If so» («если да») относится к тем, кто едет на машине, поэтому именно им нужен пропуск. «If not», «otherwise» и «but for» меняют смысл на обратный.

prompt: "I'm terrified about this exam paper, Elena." "Answer the easiest questions first, and you (to gain) confidence straight away. I used that exact trick in my own final exam; without it, I (not / to finish) the last section. Keep an eye on the clock."
explanation_ru: В первом пропуске повелительное наклонение + «and» задаёт реальный результат в будущем («will gain»), а во втором «without it» относится к прошлому экзамену, поэтому нужно «wouldn't have finished».

prompt: Dear Sir, Your builders are still painting the mountain cabin outside Innsbruck, though my family arrives on Friday. Please confirm that the rooms will be ready; if not, I (to cancel) our booking and ask for my deposit back. If it (not / to be) for your strict deposit rule, we would move to another hotel straight away. I paid early because your listing promised a finished cabin; otherwise, I (not / to choose) this place. Please reply before noon so we can plan our trip. Regards, Liam.
explanation_ru: Первый пропуск — реальное будущее решение после «if not» («will cancel»); второй — нереальное условие в настоящем «if it weren't for»; третий — нереальный результат в прошлом после «otherwise» («would not have chosen»).

prompt: Our bus climbed a narrow mountain road in the Andes full of sharp bends. "Stay seated around the corners," Miguel called out, "and we (to arrive) in the village safely." Halfway up, a falling rock blocked the lane, and but for Miguel's calm steering, the bus (to hit) the stone barrier. I still admire his skill: without such a steady driver, I (not / to try) that mountain route again. In the end, everyone stepped off the bus without a single scratch.
explanation_ru: После повелительного наклонения с «and» идёт реальное будущее («will arrive»), «but for» в прошлом эпизоде требует «would have hit», а «without» для воображаемой повторной поездки — «would not try».

prompt: Put the words in the right order to make a park notice.
answer: Leave the park before sunset; otherwise, Achieng will lock all gates.
accepted_answers: Leave the park before sunset; otherwise, Achieng will lock all gates.
explanation_ru: Повелительное наклонение ставится в первой части, затем после точки с запятой идёт «otherwise,» и реальное последствие в будущем времени.

prompt: Arrange the words into a sentence about the Seoul canteen.
answer: But for Ms Park's helpful warning, we would have missed lunch completely.
accepted_answers: But for Ms Park's helpful warning, we would have missed lunch completely.
explanation_ru: Предложный оборот «But for» + существительное открывает предложение, а в главной части следует нереальный результат в прошлом «would have missed».

prompt: Mr Tanaka posted a notice at our Osaka factory because the main entrance is closed for repairs. Follow the yellow signs to the side gate; ___, you might walk straight into the repair area. Show your staff card at the side gate, ___ the guard will open the barrier for you. Remember to carry your pass, because ___ it, nobody can enter the factory yard. Perhaps you are expecting a heavy delivery; ___, please tell Mr Tanaka before noon.
explanation_ru: «Otherwise» вводит нежелательное последствие, «and» после повелительного наклонения — положительный результат, «without» ставится перед местоимением «it», а «in that case» отсылает к названной ситуации.

prompt: Ms Weber's notice at Frankfurt airport says the express train will not run next weekend, so passengers should check whether it has restarted; ___, they must board the replacement bus outside Hall B. She also explains that ___ an extra half hour in your schedule, you can pass security calmly. I used that replacement bus during a shutdown last winter. I left my hotel early; ___, I would have missed my flight home. Honestly, ___ Ms Weber's clear signs along the corridor, I would have walked into the wrong terminal.
explanation_ru: «If not» означает «если поезд не пошёл», «with» вводит положительное условие с существительным, «otherwise» — нереальное следствие в прошлом, а «if it hadn't been for» — «если бы не» перед существительным в прошлом.
